A1.justification: Both ten-page PDFs describe BrepGaussian and provide readable text, equations, tables and figures for comparison. Neither contains an appendix. Both mention separate supplementary material that is absent from the supplied files.

before.justification: Section 4 reports original segmentation and CAD reconstruction experiments, component ablations in Tables 1–5, and qualitative ABC-NEF and ABO results.

after.justification: Section 4 retains original experimental results and adds a mask-quality ablation in Table 6 and qualitative evaluation using smartphone photographs.

M1.justification: The core two-stage Gaussian learning, losses, sampling and primitive-fitting procedure remain unchanged. Section 4.3 adds an evaluated automatic-mask variant using fine-tuned SAM instead of manual mask correction, a limited adaptation of the preparation pipeline.

E1.justification: ABC-NEF and ABO evaluation remain. Section 4.4 and Figure 7 add smartphone photographs, extending evaluation to an additional image-capture setting while retaining the CAD reconstruction task.

E2.justification: Tables 1–3 retain their comparator sets. However, v1 Figure 7 compares against Split-and-Fit and Point2CAD using the authors' labels, whereas v2 Figure 7 shows only input views and BrepGaussian meshes. Those real-world baseline comparisons are removed.

E3.justification: Section 4.3 revises the reported view-count conditions from 5/10/30/50 to 20/30/40/50, with different examples in Figure 6. Table 6 introduces manual-correction, fine-tuned-SAM and vanilla-SAM preparation conditions. Existing evaluation metrics and main experimental settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: New Table 6 tests sensitivity to mask preparation and the accuracy cost of automation. Figure 6 revises the view-count sensitivity analysis with different examples and conditions. Existing component ablations in Tables 4–5 are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, uncertainty intervals or significance tests. New Table 6 continues the existing practice of reporting single summary values.

E6.justification: Tables 1–5 are numerically unchanged. Table 6 adds F1 values of 0.8941/0.8621/0.8259 and Dc entries of 5.04/5.33/5.66, respectively, for manual correction/fine-tuned SAM/vanilla SAM. Figures 6–7 replace qualitative results; these do not establish same-setting performance gains between versions.

T1.justification: Equations 1–14 retain the same Gaussian rendering, loss and evaluation definitions. No formal assumptions, derivations, theorems or proofs are added or substantively revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the claims of complete B-Rep reconstruction from multi-view images without point-cloud supervision, two-stage learning and constraint-guided fitting. Removing 'significantly' from the conclusion's performance statement does not change its substantive claim.

C2.justification: New Section 4.5 explicitly identifies reconstructed point and label quality as limiting performance on complex objects and acknowledges pipeline complexity. Section 4.3 newly interprets fine-tuned SAM as enabling automation with a small accuracy cost.

D1.justification: V1's promise to release code and datasets upon acceptance is deleted without replacement access information. Existing implementation details remain; the added SAM fine-tuning experiment provides no corresponding training recipe. This does not establish that previously available resources were withdrawn.

R1.justification: Section 2.1 adds citations to GenCAD, CADdreamer, HOLA and Img2CAD, with a brief statement about limitations of image-conditioned CAD generation. Existing related-work coverage and the principal novelty positioning remain.

P1.justification: Limited edits standardize B-Rep and stage terminology, remove the stray reference to a linear Consistency metric while retaining F1, revise affiliations, and add acknowledgments and a Limitations subsection. Conclusions becomes Section 5. Most prose and the overall narrative remain unchanged.

P2.justification: Table 6 is added, Figures 6–7 are replaced, and Figure 7 changes from a baseline-comparison grid to a views/meshes gallery. Tables 1–2 move from page 8 to page 7, Figure 3 changes position, and the author block is compacted. The overall visual format remains intact.

improvement.justification: Table 6 adds useful evidence about dependence on manual mask correction, an issue v1 disclosed but did not test. Smartphone examples and explicit applicability limits make the practical evaluation modestly more informative. These gains are constrained by unspecified SAM fine-tuning details, removal of Figure 7's baseline comparisons, and deletion of the release promise; the core quantitative evidence remains unchanged.
